questions.title: Simple Bank Account
questions.objective: Implement deposit, withdraw, and balance check on account instance.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class BankAccount that keeps the money of one person.
• __init__(self, owner, balance=0) stores the owner's name and the starting balance in instance attributes
• deposit(self, amount): adds amount to the balance and returns True. If amount <= 0, it changes nothing and returns False
• withdraw(self, amount): takes amount from the balance and returns True. If amount <= 0 or amount is bigger than the balance, it changes nothing and returns False
• get_balance(self): returns the current balance

The program creates one account and runs the commands:
• DEPOSIT x → print OK if the deposit worked, otherwise FAILED
• WITHDRAW x → print OK if the withdrawal worked, otherwise FAILED
• BALANCE → print the balance

Example: an account for Asha with 100, then DEPOSIT 50, WITHDRAW 500, BALANCE prints OK, FAILED, 150.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the owner's name and the starting balance (an integer), separated by a space.
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One output line for every command, as described.
hints: Store the values with self.owner = owner and self.balance = balance inside __init__.
Check the bad cases first in withdraw: if amount <= 0 or amount > self.balance: return False.
In the driver, split each command: parts = input().split(), then compare parts[0] with 'DEPOSIT', 'WITHDRAW' and 'BALANCE'.

questions.title: Rectangle Geometry Class
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Rectangle.
• __init__(self, width, height) stores the two sides
• area(self) returns width * height
• perimeter(self) returns 2 * (width + height)
• resize(self, width, height) changes both sides
• __str__(self) returns the text Rectangle(width=W, height=H), so that print(rect) shows the sides

The program creates one rectangle and runs the commands:
• AREA → print the area
• PERIMETER → print the perimeter
• PRINT → print(rect), which uses __str__
• RESIZE w h → change the sides (prints nothing)

Example: a 3 x 4 rectangle with AREA, PERIMETER, PRINT prints 12, 14 and Rectangle(width=3, height=4).
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the width and the height (integers), separated by a space.
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One output line for every AREA, PERIMETER and PRINT command. RESIZE prints nothing.
hints: __str__ must RETURN a string, not print it: return f'Rectangle(width={self.width}, height={self.height})'.
print(rect) calls rect.__str__() for you.
resize only needs to assign new values to self.width and self.height.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the width and the height (integers), separated by a space.
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
extra_fields.output_format: One output line for every AREA, PERIMETER and PRINT command. RESIZE prints nothing.

questions.title: Circle Geometry with Check
questions.objective: Enforce radius > 0; calculate area and circumference (pi = 3.14159).
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Circle that never holds an invalid radius. Use PI = 3.14159 as a class attribute.
• __init__(self, radius) stores the radius. If radius <= 0, raise ValueError
• set_radius(self, radius) changes the radius. If radius <= 0, raise ValueError and keep the old radius
• area(self) returns PI * radius * radius
• circumference(self) returns 2 * PI * radius

The program reads the starting radius. If creating the circle raises ValueError, it prints INVALID RADIUS and stops. Otherwise it runs the commands:
• AREA → print the area with 2 decimal places
• CIRCUMFERENCE → print the circumference with 2 decimal places
• SET r → change the radius. If it raises ValueError, print INVALID RADIUS (the circle keeps its old radius); otherwise print nothing

Example: radius 1 with AREA, CIRCUMFERENCE prints 3.14 and 6.28.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the starting radius (a number).
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
If the starting radius is invalid, the command lines are still given but not used.
questions.output_format: INVALID RADIUS if the starting radius is invalid. Otherwise one line for every AREA and CIRCUMFERENCE command, and INVALID RADIUS for every rejected SET. Numbers are printed with 2 decimal places.
hints: raise ValueError('radius must be positive') stops __init__ before the object is created.
Wrap the creation in try / except ValueError in the driver.
Check the new radius BEFORE assigning it in set_radius, so the old value stays when it is invalid. Print with f'{value:.2f}'.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the starting radius (a number).
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).

extra_fields.output_format: INVALID RADIUS if the starting radius is invalid. Otherwise one line for every AREA and CIRCUMFERENCE command, and INVALID RADIUS for every rejected SET. Numbers are printed with 2 decimal places.

questions.title: Student Grade Tracker
questions.objective: Add subject grades to instance list; compute average and letter grade.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Student that collects grades.
• __init__(self, name) stores the name and starts an EMPTY list of grades for this student
• add_grade(self, subject, grade) adds (subject, grade) to the list and returns True. If the grade is not between 0 and 100, it adds nothing and returns False
• average(self) returns the average grade, or None when there are no grades
• letter(self) returns A (average >= 90), B (>= 80), C (>= 70), D (>= 60) or F, or None when there are no grades

The program creates one student and runs the commands:
• ADD subject grade → print OK or INVALID
• AVERAGE → print the average with 2 decimal places, or NO GRADES
• LETTER → print the letter, or NO GRADES
• COUNT → print how many grades were added

Example: ADD math 95, ADD art 80, AVERAGE, LETTER prints OK, OK, 87.50, B.

questions.title: __str__ vs __repr__ Dunder
questions.objective: Implement __str__ for display and __repr__ for unambiguous representation.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: __str__ gives a friendly text for users, and __repr__ gives an exact text for programmers, ideally one that looks like the code that creates the object.

Write a class Book with title, author and year.
• __str__(self) returns: <title> by <author> (<year>), for example Dune by Frank Herbert (1965)
• __repr__(self) returns: Book(<title repr>, <author repr>, <year>), for example Book('Dune', 'Frank Herbert', 1965). Use !r in the f-string so the strings get quotes
• set_year(self, year) changes the year

The program creates one book and runs the commands:
• STR → print(book), which uses __str__
• REPR → print(repr(book))
• LIST → print([book]). A list shows its items with __repr__, not __str__
• YEAR y → change the year (prints nothing)

Example: for Dune, Frank Herbert, 1965 the commands STR, REPR print Dune by Frank Herbert (1965) and Book('Dune', 'Frank Herbert', 1965).
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the title.
Line 2: the author.
Line 3: the year (integer).
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One output line for every STR, REPR and LIST command. YEAR prints nothing.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of title, author <= 100
0 <= year <= 3000
1 <= Q <= 100
sample_outputs:
Dune by Frank Herbert (1965)
Book('Dune', 'Frank Herbert', 1965)
hints: Both methods must return strings, not print them.
f'{self.title!r}' gives 'Dune' with quotes; the year needs no !r because it is a number.
print([book]) calls repr() on every item inside the list.

questions.title: Class vs Instance Attributes
questions.objective: Demonstrate distinction between class-level counter and instance IDs.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A class attribute belongs to the class and is shared by all objects. An instance attribute belongs to one object.

Write a class Ticket.
• Class attribute: count = 0, the number of tickets created so far
• __init__(self, name): add 1 to Ticket.count (the class attribute, not self.count), then store the instance attributes self.id = Ticket.count and self.name = name
• __str__(self) returns Ticket <id>: <name>

The program keeps all tickets in a dictionary by id and runs the commands:
• NEW name → create a ticket and print Created ticket <id> for <name>
• COUNT → print Ticket.count
• SHOW id → print the ticket (using __str__), or NOT FOUND

Example: NEW Asha, NEW Ben, COUNT, SHOW 1 prints Created ticket 1 for Asha, Created ticket 2 for Ben, 2, Ticket 1: Asha.

Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One output line for every command, as described.
questions.constraints:
1 <= Q <= 1000
Names are words without spaces
-10^6 <= id in SHOW <= 10^6

Read the new value with Ticket.count right after increasing it.
tickets[ticket.id] = ticket stores each ticket; use tickets.get(id) or the in operator for SHOW.

questions.title: Mutable Class Attribute Trap
questions.objective: Contrast shared mutable class attribute against per-instance attributes.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A list written at class level is created ONCE and shared by every object of the class. Appending to it through one object changes it for all of them. A list created in __init__ belongs to one object only.

Write two classes:
• BadTeam: members = [] at class level (the trap). __init__(self, name) only stores the name. add(self, person) appends to self.members
• GoodTeam: __init__(self, name) stores the name and creates self.members = []. add(self, person) appends to self.members

The program runs the commands:
• CREATE name → create a BadTeam and a GoodTeam with this name
• ADD name person → add the person to both versions of that team
• SHOW name → print two lines: bad: <members of the BadTeam> and good: <members of the GoodTeam>, each as a Python list

Example: CREATE red, CREATE blue, ADD red Asha, SHOW blue prints bad: ['Asha'] and good: [], because all BadTeams share one list.

Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description). Every ADD and SHOW uses a team created earlier.
questions.output_format: Two lines for every SHOW command, as described. CREATE and ADD print nothing.
questions.constraints:
1 <= Q <= 1000
Team names and person names are words without spaces
Team names are different

questions.title: Digital Wallet Balance
questions.objective: Manage wallet balance with credit, debit, fee checks, and transaction logs.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Wallet with a balance (starting at 0) and a transaction log.
• Keep the balance in a "private" attribute self._balance and read it through a method balance(self). The leading underscore tells other code not to change it directly
• credit(self, amount): if amount <= 0 return 'INVALID'. Otherwise add it, log CREDIT <amount> and return 'OK'
• debit(self, amount): if amount <= 0 return 'INVALID'. Every debit costs a fee: fee = max(1, amount // 50) (2%, at least 1). If amount + fee is more than the balance, log DECLINED <amount> and return 'DECLINED'. Otherwise take amount + fee from the balance, log DEBIT <amount> FEE <fee> and return 'OK'
• history(self) returns the list of log lines (INVALID commands are not logged)

The program creates a wallet and runs the commands:
• CREDIT x → print the result of credit
• DEBIT x → print the result of debit
• BALANCE → print the balance
• HISTORY → print every log line in order, or NO TRANSACTIONS if the log is empty

Example: CREDIT 100, DEBIT 50, BALANCE prints OK, OK, 49 (50 + fee 1 were taken).
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One line for every CREDIT, DEBIT and BALANCE command. HISTORY prints one line per log entry, or NO TRANSACTIONS.
hints: Compute the fee first: fee = max(1, amount // 50). 100 // 50 is 2, and 30 // 50 is 0, so max gives 1.
Compare amount + fee with the balance, not just amount.
Append strings like f'DEBIT {amount} FEE {fee}' to self._log.

questions.title: Shopping Cart Aggregator
questions.objective: Add, remove, and calculate total cost of item objects with quantities.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write two classes.

Item:
• __init__(self, name, price, qty) stores the three values
• subtotal(self) returns price * qty

Cart:
• __init__(self) creates an empty dictionary of items by name (it keeps the order items were first added)
• add(self, name, price, qty): if the item is already in the cart, add qty to it and keep its old price. Otherwise create a new Item
• remove(self, name, qty): if the item is not in the cart, return False. Otherwise take qty away; if nothing is left (qty >= current quantity), delete the item. Return True
• total(self) returns the sum of all subtotals

The program runs the commands:
• ADD name price qty → add (prints nothing)
• REMOVE name qty → print OK, or NOT FOUND
• TOTAL → print the total with 2 decimal places
• LIST → print one line per item: <name> x<qty> @ <price with 2 decimals>, or EMPTY

Example: ADD apple 0.50 4, ADD milk 2.25 1, TOTAL prints 4.25.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each. Prices are decimal numbers and quantities are positive integers.
questions.output_format: One line for every REMOVE and TOTAL command, and the item lines (or EMPTY) for every LIST command.
questions.constraints:
1 <= Q <= 1000
0 <= price <= 10^4
1 <= qty <= 10^4
Item names are words without spaces
hints: Store Item objects in a dict: self.items[name] = Item(name, price, qty).
total can be sum(item.subtotal() for item in self.items.values()).
del self.items[name] removes an item when its quantity reaches 0.

questions.title: Temperature Unit Container
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Temperature that stores one value together with its unit, C (Celsius), F (Fahrenheit) or K (Kelvin).
• __init__(self, value, unit) stores both
• to_celsius(self), to_fahrenheit(self) and to_kelvin(self) return the temperature in that unit
• set(self, value, unit) replaces the stored temperature

Formulas:
• C = (F - 32) * 5 / 9 and F = C * 9 / 5 + 32
• K = C + 273.15 and C = K - 273.15
Tip: convert the stored value to Celsius first inside every method, then from Celsius to the target unit.

The program creates one temperature and runs the commands:
• C, F or K → print the temperature in that unit with 2 decimal places
• SET value unit → replace the temperature (prints nothing)

Example: for 100 C the commands F, K print 212.00 and 373.15.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: a value (a number) and a unit (C, F or K), separated by a space.
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One line for every C, F and K command, with 2 decimal places. SET prints nothing.
hints: to_celsius handles three cases with if / elif / else on self.unit.
to_fahrenheit can be self.to_celsius() * 9 / 5 + 32, and to_kelvin can be self.to_celsius() + 273.15.
Print with f'{value:.2f}'. Values very close to 0 may print as -0.00 for a tiny negative number, so the tests avoid those cases.

questions.title: Circular Playlist Navigator
questions.objective: Add songs, track active index, and wrap .next_track() to beginning.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Playlist.
• __init__(self) creates an empty list of songs and sets the active index to 0
• add(self, song) appends a song. The first song added becomes the current song
• current(self) returns the current song, or None if the playlist is empty
• next_track(self) moves to the next song and returns it. After the last song it wraps around to the first one. Returns None if the playlist is empty
• prev_track(self) moves to the previous song and returns it. Before the first song it wraps around to the last one. Returns None if the playlist is empty

The program runs the commands:
• ADD song → add the song (the song name is the rest of the line and may contain spaces; prints nothing)
• CURRENT, NEXT, PREV → print the song, or EMPTY

Example: ADD A, ADD B, NEXT, NEXT prints B and then A (it wrapped around).

Next Q lines: one command each (see the description).
questions.output_format: One line for every CURRENT, NEXT and PREV command.

1 <= length of a song name <= 100

questions.title: Library Book Ledger
questions.objective: Track availability, borrower names, and return status across titles.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Library that tracks which titles are on the shelf and who has borrowed the others.
• __init__(self) creates an empty dictionary: title → borrower name, or None when the book is available
• add_book(self, title) returns 'ADDED', or 'EXISTS' if the title is already there
• borrow(self, name, title) returns 'NOT FOUND' for an unknown title, 'UNAVAILABLE' if it is already borrowed, otherwise records the borrower and returns 'OK'
• return_book(self, title) returns 'NOT FOUND' for an unknown title, 'NOT BORROWED' if it is on the shelf, otherwise marks it available and returns 'OK'
• status(self, title) returns 'available', 'borrowed by <name>' or 'NOT FOUND'

The program runs the commands (titles are the rest of the line and may contain spaces):
• ADD title, BORROW name title, RETURN title, STATUS title → print the method's result
• REPORT → print one line per title in the order they were added: <title>: <status>, or EMPTY

Example: ADD Dune, BORROW Asha Dune, STATUS Dune prints ADDED, OK, borrowed by Asha.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each. In BORROW the first word after the command is the borrower's name and the rest is the title.
questions.output_format: One line for every ADD, BORROW, RETURN and STATUS command; the report lines (or EMPTY) for every REPORT.
questions.constraints:
1 <= Q <= 1000
Borrower names are words without spaces
1 <= length of a title <= 100
sample_inputs:
3
ADD Dune
BORROW Asha Dune
STATUS Dune

questions.title: Vector2D Arithmetic
questions.objective: Implement 2D vector class with .add(), .dot(), and .magnitude() methods.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Vector2D for 2D vectors with integer coordinates.
• __init__(self, x, y) stores the coordinates
• add(self, other) returns a NEW Vector2D: (x1 + x2, y1 + y2). It does not change self or other
• dot(self, other) returns the dot product x1 * x2 + y1 * y2
• magnitude(self) returns the length sqrt(x^2 + y^2) (use math.sqrt or ** 0.5)
• __repr__(self) returns Vector2D(x, y)

The program runs the commands:
• ADD x1 y1 x2 y2 → print the sum vector (using __repr__)
• DOT x1 y1 x2 y2 → print the dot product
• MAG x y → print the magnitude with 3 decimal places

Example: ADD 1 2 3 4 prints Vector2D(4, 6), DOT 1 2 3 4 prints 11, and MAG 3 4 prints 5.000.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each, with integer coordinates.
questions.output_format: One output line for every command, as described.
hints: add creates and returns a new object: return Vector2D(self.x + other.x, self.y + other.y).
other is another Vector2D, so you can read other.x and other.y.
print(vector) uses __repr__ when the class has no __str__.

extra_fields.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each, with integer coordinates.
extra_fields.output_format: One output line for every command, as described.

questions.title: Rate Limiter Counter
questions.objective: Enforce max K actions per window using simulated input tick timestamps.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A rate limiter stops a user from doing too many actions in a short time. Write a class RateLimiter.
• __init__(self, k, window): at most k actions per user are allowed in any time window of length window
• allow(self, user, t): a user tries an action at time t. Look at the user's ALLOWED actions with a time in the range (t - window, t], that is, later than t - window and up to t. If there are fewer than k of them, record this action at time t and return True. Otherwise return False (blocked actions are not recorded)
• usage(self, user, t) returns how many allowed actions of the user are in (t - window, t]
• Each user has their own limit. Keep a collections.deque of allowed times for each user, and remove times from the left when they are too old (<= t - window)

Times in the input never go down. The program reads k and window, then runs the commands:
• REQ user t → print ALLOWED or BLOCKED
• USAGE user t → print the number of allowed actions in the window ending at t

Example with k = 2 and window = 10: REQ a 1, REQ a 5, REQ a 9, REQ a 11 prints ALLOWED, ALLOWED, BLOCKED, ALLOWED (at t = 11 the action at time 1 is out of the window (1, 11]).
questions.input_format:
Line 1: two integers k and window.
Next line: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description). Times never decrease from one command to the next.
questions.output_format: One output line for every command, as described.
questions.constraints:
1 <= k <= 1000
1 <= window <= 10^9
1 <= Q <= 10^5
0 <= t <= 10^9
User names are words without spaces
sample_inputs:

4
REQ a 1
REQ a 5
REQ a 9
REQ a 11

1 5
4
REQ x 0
REQ x 4
REQ x 5
USAGE x 5
hints: from collections import deque; self.times = {} maps each user to a deque of allowed times.
Write a small helper _clean(user, t) that pops from the left while times[0] <= t - window. Both allow and usage call it.
An action exactly at time t - window is outside the window, because the window starts after t - window.

questions.title: Course Prerequisite Checker
questions.objective: Model courses preventing enrollment until prerequisites are finished.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write two classes.

Course:
• __init__(self, code, prereqs) stores the course code and the list of prerequisite codes

Student:
• __init__(self, name) creates an empty set of completed courses and an empty set of enrolled courses
• enroll(self, course) returns:
- 'ALREADY COMPLETED' if the student completed it
- 'ALREADY ENROLLED' if the student is enrolled in it now
- 'MISSING <codes>' if some prerequisites are not completed, listing the missing codes in the order the course lists them, separated by spaces
- otherwise it enrolls the student and returns 'ENROLLED'
• complete(self, code) moves the course from enrolled to completed and returns 'COMPLETED', or returns 'NOT ENROLLED'

The program keeps courses and students in dictionaries. A student is created the first time their name appears. Commands:
• COURSE code p1 p2 ... → define a course with zero or more prerequisites (prints nothing)
• ENROLL name code → print UNKNOWN COURSE if the course was never defined, otherwise the result of enroll
• COMPLETE name code → print the result of complete
• STATUS name → print completed: <codes> | enrolled: <codes>, each list sorted alphabetically and separated by spaces, or none if empty

Example: COURSE CS101, COURSE CS201 CS101, ENROLL amy CS201 prints MISSING CS101.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description). Codes and names are words without spaces.
questions.output_format: One output line for every ENROLL, COMPLETE and STATUS command. COURSE prints nothing.
questions.constraints:
1 <= Q <= 1000
0 <= prerequisites per course <= 10
A course is defined at most once
sample_inputs:
3
COURSE CS101
COURSE CS201 CS101
ENROLL amy CS201

6
COURSE A
COURSE B A
ENROLL bo A
COMPLETE bo A
ENROLL bo B
STATUS bo
sample_outputs:
ENROLLED
COMPLETED
ENROLLED
completed: A | enrolled: B
hints: [p for p in course.prereqs if p not in self.completed] gives the missing prerequisites in order.
Use sets for completed and enrolled: self.enrolled.remove(code) and self.completed.add(code) in complete().
students.setdefault(name, Student(name)) works, but creates a throw-away object each time; if name not in students: students[name] = Student(name) is clearer.

questions.title: Stock Alert Inventory
questions.objective: Track SKU counts and trigger alerts when stock drops below threshold.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a class Inventory that tracks the stock of each SKU (product code) and warns when it gets low.
• add_sku(self, sku, qty, threshold) adds a new SKU and returns 'OK', or 'EXISTS' if it is already there
• restock(self, sku, qty) adds qty and returns 'OK', or 'NOT FOUND'
• sell(self, sku, qty) returns 'NOT FOUND' for an unknown SKU, 'INSUFFICIENT' if qty is more than the stock (nothing changes), otherwise removes qty and returns 'OK'
• Alert rule: a SKU is LOW when its stock is below its threshold. When a sale moves a SKU from not-low to LOW, the sale also produces the alert line ALERT <sku> <stock>. A SKU that is already LOW gives no new alert on later sales. A restock that brings it back to stock >= threshold makes it not-low again, so a later drop alerts again
• A SKU added with a quantity already below its threshold starts as LOW, without an alert

The program runs the commands:
• ADD sku qty threshold, RESTOCK sku qty → print the result
• SELL sku qty → print the result, and on the next line the ALERT line if there is one
• REPORT → print one line per SKU in the order they were added: <sku> <stock>, with the word LOW added at the end if the SKU is low; or EMPTY

Example: ADD pen 10 5, SELL pen 6 prints OK, then OK and ALERT pen 4.
questions.input_format:
Line 1: the number of commands Q.
Next Q lines: one command each (see the description). SKUs are words without spaces; quantities and thresholds are non-negative integers.
questions.output_format: One line for every ADD and RESTOCK, one or two lines for every SELL, and the report lines (or EMPTY) for every REPORT.
hints: Store per SKU a small dict or object: stock, threshold and a flag low.
In sell, compute was_low before changing the stock and is_low after. Alert only when not was_low and is_low.
Let sell return two values, such as ('OK', 'ALERT pen 4') or ('OK', None), and let the driver print the second one when it is not None.
